thesis: The 6 September memo said stay flat because the FOMC was a coin flip nobody at this desk can call. That has become literally true - hike and hold are now within a point of each other - and the resolving event has a date: August CPI on the morning of 11 September. There is no version of buying index beta 48 hours before that print that is an edge.
bull_case: The trend has still not broken: packet close 762.4 with close > SMA50 > SMA200 and 63d momentum +3.7%, and ATR of 0.7% remains the lowest in the book. The hawkish outcome is genuinely not settled - the probability of a hold has risen to about 50.6% from 43% a week ago, and Governor Waller said on 3 September he was inclined to support holding at 3.5-3.75%. The economy underneath is not rolling over: 162,000 jobs added in August with unemployment steady at 4.1%. A hold on 16 September with a soft CPI two days earlier is the setup that takes this straight back to the highs.
bear_case: A coin flip with a two-day fuse is the definition of no edge, and the tape agrees: RSI has fallen to 43, 63d momentum is +3.7% and the score is +0.39, so the index is drifting while the Fed argument runs. We are -1.1% on the position. Yields keep grinding against it - the 10-year at 4.796% and the 2-year at 4.394% on 8 September, the 2-year at its highest since January 2025. The energy impulse feeding the inflation problem is still live with crude spiking 5% to $90 on Hormuz strikes. And the concentration objection has not changed: AI-linked names are roughly 40-45% of index capitalisation, so SPY is not the diversifier it is bought as. September remains the weakest month seasonally.
catalysts: August CPI on the morning of 11 Sep 2026
15-16 Sep 2026 FOMC decision and dot plot
risks: Binary event risk 48 hours out with odds at roughly 50/50
A hawkish hike with the 10-year through 5%
AI concentration: an AI drawdown is an index drawdown
Energy-led inflation re-accelerating on Hormuz disruption
invalidation: Unchanged in structure from 6 Sep, with the levels re-anchored: flips long on a weekly close above 790 made after the 16 Sep FOMC rather than before it; the risk case confirms on a close below 740, which breaks the SMA50 and the summer range.
